title: Only 7% Pass This Midwifery Entrance Exam
summary: Pregnancy, labour, newborn care, safety and compassionate judgement combine in one focused entrance challenge.

landing.intro: Pregnancy, birth, newborn care and calm judgement—how much would you remember when every detail matters?
landing.startNote: Short ad first - then it begins.

about.body:
This worldwide entertainment challenge explores entrance-level midwifery knowledge across 40 varied questions. It covers pregnancy physiology, antenatal wellbeing, labour, newborn care, infection prevention and respectful communication.

The five challenges become progressively more applied, moving from a first appointment into pregnancy and birth foundations, respectful safety, labour and newborn decisions, and a final integrated birth-centre assessment. Questions stay at recognition and judgement level rather than teaching diagnosis or treatment.

Your final percentage reflects only the answers given in this entertainment quiz. It is a playful snapshot of the maternity-care areas that felt strongest and the topics that proved more challenging, not a judgement of clinical competence or suitability for midwifery practice.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Work through each maternity-care challenge at your own pace—there is no timer or speed bonus.
Choose the single option best supported by the visible information. Correctness stays hidden until the final reveal.
Keep going as the scenarios become harder, then reveal your score and complete answer review.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited midwifery entrance examination, clinical assessment, professional qualification or medical advice. Maternity-care procedures and responsibilities vary; always follow local policy and qualified clinical guidance.

profiles.title: The Birth Centre Standout
profiles.copy: You combined strong maternity knowledge with calm, respectful judgement from the first appointment to the final handover. Subtle changes, safety priorities and person-centred choices stayed clear even as the cases became more demanding.

profiles.title: The Midwifery Natural
profiles.copy: You showed an excellent feel for pregnancy, birth and newborn-care foundations. Most of the observation, communication and handover traps did not pull you away from the safest supported answer.

profiles.title: The Calm Candidate
profiles.copy: You handled a broad mix of maternity knowledge and compassionate decisions with steady reasoning. A few finer details kept the entrance challenge interesting.

profiles.title: The Thoughtful Observer
profiles.copy: You built a solid result by noticing important clues and treating dignity and safety seriously. Your strongest stage shows where your maternity-care instincts are already taking shape.

profiles.title: The Promising Applicant
profiles.copy: You solved a good share of the birth-centre challenge and showed useful instincts across several care areas. The answer review will reveal which foundations are ready for another look.

profiles.title: The Curious Care Advocate
profiles.copy: The challenge uncovered some knowledge gaps, but it also found moments of thoughtful and respectful judgement. Every explanation offers a fresh chance to strengthen the foundations behind safe maternity care.

details.analysisTitle: How to read your midwifery score
details.analysisCopy: This 40-question result combines pregnancy physiology, antenatal wellbeing, labour, newborn care, infection prevention and respectful communication. Each correct answer adds 2.5 percentage points.

details.positionCopy: The entertainment challenge target is 32 correct answers out of 40. Your marker shows how close this attempt came without assessing clinical competence.
details.measuredIntro: The selected questions span three broad parts of entrance-level maternity-care thinking without teaching diagnosis or treatment.

measuredAreas.title: Pregnancy and antenatal care
measuredAreas.copy: Recognising foundational physiology, meaningful changes and simple time information.

measuredAreas.title: Labour and newborn care
measuredAreas.copy: Following basic birth processes and identifying supportive newborn-care principles.

measuredAreas.title: Safety and communication
measuredAreas.copy: Protecting infection safety, dignity and compassionate communication while recognising deterioration.

details.tipsTitle: Three ways to sharpen maternity-care reasoning
details.tipsIntro: These are general quiz strategies—not clinical instruction, medical advice or a professional assessment.

tips.title: Notice change from normal
tips.copy: A clear difference from the usual pattern can matter more than comparing one person with somebody else.

tips.title: Combine the clues
tips.copy: Sudden bleeding, pallor, dizziness or a major change in wellbeing carry more weight together than separately.

tips.title: Protect dignity first
tips.copy: Strong communication choices acknowledge emotion, listen and preserve privacy without making unsupported promises.

details.finalCopy: You finished with {score} correct answers out of {total}. Your profile for this attempt is shown below.

questions.question: Which organ supports exchange during pregnancy?
questions.explanation: The placenta supports exchange of oxygen, nutrients and waste products between the maternal and fetal circulations.

questions.question: Why are observations recorded at more than one appointment?
answers: To predict an exact birth time
To notice changes and trends over time
questions.explanation: Repeated observations help reveal meaningful changes rather than relying on one isolated value.

questions.question: What does the cervix do during labour?
answers: It gradually opens as labour progresses
questions.explanation: The cervix softens, thins and opens during labour to allow birth.

questions.question: What helps a stable newborn conserve warmth soon after birth?
questions.explanation: Drying and skin-to-skin contact help reduce heat loss and support early bonding.

questions.question: When should hands be cleaned around maternity care?
answers: Only at the end of a shift
Before clean contact and after exposure risk
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene is needed at appropriate moments even when gloves are also used.

questions.question: A woman says, “I’m worried about what happens next.” What is the best first response?
answers: Acknowledge the worry and invite her questions
Say there is nothing to worry about
questions.explanation: Acknowledging emotion and listening first creates space for clear, respectful communication.

questions.question: What is one main role of amniotic fluid?
questions.explanation: Amniotic fluid surrounds and cushions the developing baby.

questions.question: A baby’s movement pattern clearly changes from usual. What matters most?
answers: Every baby must move at identical times
Take the change from normal seriously
questions.explanation: A noticeable change from the baby’s usual movement pattern warrants prompt qualified advice rather than comparison with another pregnancy.

questions.question: Where does a baby normally develop during pregnancy?
questions.explanation: The uterus expands to support the developing baby throughout pregnancy.

questions.question: What connects the baby to the placenta?
questions.explanation: The umbilical cord contains vessels connecting the baby with the placenta.

questions.question: Which sequence best represents oxygen reaching the baby?

visual.ariaLabel: Maternal blood to placenta to cord to baby

questions.explanation: Oxygen from maternal blood crosses the placenta and is carried through the umbilical cord to the baby.

questions.question: A new severe headache appears with visual changes during pregnancy. What is the safest response?
answers: Rest and reassess after an hour
Wait for the next routine appointment
Ask someone at home to keep an eye on the symptoms
Seek prompt assessment from a qualified maternity professional
questions.explanation: A new severe headache with visual changes is a concerning change that warrants prompt qualified assessment.

questions.question: A chart records 70, 74 and 78 at three visits. What does it show?
questions.explanation: Each recorded value is higher than the previous one.

questions.question: A bottle holds 1.5 L. How many millilitres is that?
questions.explanation: One litre is 1,000 mL, so 1.5 litres is 1,500 mL.

questions.question: Which organ provides the muscular contractions of labour?
questions.explanation: The muscular wall of the uterus contracts during labour.

questions.question: The baby is born but the placenta is not yet delivered. Which labour stage is this?
questions.explanation: The third stage begins after the baby is born and continues until the placenta is delivered.

questions.question: A woman becomes tearful and says she feels overwhelmed. What should happen first?
answers: Pause, acknowledge how she feels and listen
Reassure her that feeling overwhelmed is common
Try to distract her from what is upsetting her
questions.explanation: Acknowledging emotion and listening is more supportive than dismissal, comparison or unsupported reassurance.

questions.question: Equipment’s sterile wrapper is torn before use. What is the safest response?
answers: Do not treat it as sterile; replace or escalate appropriately
Touch the contents to test them
questions.explanation: A damaged sterile barrier cannot be relied upon and should not be used as though intact.

questions.question: A clean procedure is about to begin. What is essential immediately beforehand?
answers: Skip cleaning if hands look clean
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene immediately before a clean or aseptic task helps prevent harmful germs entering the body.

questions.question: A task may splash body fluid towards the eyes. What is the safest preparation?
answers: Wear ordinary glasses as the only protection
Use appropriate eye or face protection
questions.explanation: Protection should match the stated exposure risk, including eye or face protection when splashing is possible.

questions.question: A woman says she does not want students present. What is the best response?
answers: Tell her attendance removes that choice
Discuss her refusal in the corridor
Respect her decision and protect her privacy
questions.explanation: The person receiving care can decline additional observers and should have privacy protected.

questions.question: A woman asks to consider her options before deciding. What is the respectful response?
answers: Pressure her into the quickest option
Treat questions as refusal of care
Give clear information, answer questions and allow appropriate time
questions.explanation: Informed choice requires understandable information and freedom from pressure.

questions.question: Before an examination, what should happen first?
answers: Explain it clearly and obtain informed agreement
questions.explanation: Respectful care requires clear information, opportunity for questions and informed consent.

questions.question: Before touching a newborn after handling shared equipment, what is required?
answers: Waiting until the end of the day
questions.explanation: Clean hands help reduce transmission of harmful germs to newborns.

questions.question: Which change matters most?
answers: The time printed on the chart
The fact that labour began earlier
The combined feverish feeling, shaking and marked change from earlier
questions.explanation: A major change with feeling feverish and shaking requires prompt qualified assessment rather than routine delay.

items: NOW::Feels feverish · shaking · suddenly much worse
visual.ariaLabel: Earlier comfortable and alert. Now feels feverish, is shaking and suddenly feels much worse.

questions.question: Which behaviour can be an early feeding cue?
answers: Turning the head and opening the mouth
questions.explanation: Rooting, mouth opening and hand-to-mouth movements can signal readiness to feed.

questions.question: What is the basic aim of skin-to-skin contact for a stable newborn?
answers: Support warmth, calm contact and early feeding
questions.explanation: Skin-to-skin contact supports thermal care, bonding and early feeding while appropriate observation continues.

questions.question: Which visible pattern is most useful when describing contractions?
answers: Their frequency, duration and change over time
questions.explanation: Frequency, duration and how the pattern changes give useful descriptive information.

questions.question: What normally happens to the cervix as labour progresses?
questions.explanation: During labour the cervix effaces and dilates.

questions.question: Why can changing position during labour be helpful when safe and comfortable?
answers: It guarantees an exact birth time
It can support comfort and individual coping
It removes the need for observation
questions.explanation: Movement and position choice may support comfort, but individual needs and circumstances vary.

questions.question: Why is a stable newborn dried soon after birth?
answers: To remove the need for contact
questions.explanation: Drying removes moisture that would otherwise increase heat loss.

questions.question: A newborn is not feeding as usual and is breathing noticeably faster. What is safest?
answers: Wait several days without telling anyone
Recognise the change and seek prompt qualified assessment
questions.explanation: Poor feeding with a breathing change is concerning and needs qualified assessment, not self-treatment.

questions.question: Who needs immediate attention?
answers: Person A, because routine questions are quicker
Both can wait for the next handover
Person B, because sudden bleeding, pallor and dizziness show deterioration
questions.explanation: The combined sudden changes for Person B outweigh Person A’s stable routine need.

items: PERSON A::Comfortable · alert · routine feeding question
PERSON B::New heavy bleeding · pale · dizzy
visual.ariaLabel: Person A is comfortable and alert with a routine feeding question. Person B has new heavy bleeding and is pale and dizzy.

questions.question: How should a clean, dry umbilical cord stump generally be treated?
answers: Keep it clean and dry and seek advice if concerning changes appear
Pull it to make it detach
questions.explanation: Basic cord care focuses on cleanliness and dryness, with qualified review for concerning change.

questions.question: Which observation changed?
questions.context: Handover note — 14:00: comfortable breathing. 15:00: breathing noticeably faster; other recorded details unchanged.
answers: Breathing changed from comfortable to noticeably faster
questions.explanation: The handover shows a clear change in breathing between the two observations.

questions.question: Which explanation best links both observations?
questions.context: The placenta is the exchange organ. A diagram now shows reduced transfer across it and less oxygen in the cord.
answers: Reduced placental exchange can mean less oxygen reaches the baby
The stomach supplies the cord directly
questions.explanation: The placenta supports exchange; reduced exchange can reduce oxygen transfer to the baby.

questions.question: What total and trend should be handed over?
questions.context: Fluid chart: 650 mL + 450 mL. Observation chart: earlier 74, latest 82.
answers: 1,100 mL total, with the latest observation higher than the first
1,650 mL total with a falling trend
questions.explanation: 650 mL plus 450 mL is 1,100 mL, and 82 is higher than 74.

questions.question: What is the safest conclusion?
questions.context: Earlier: regular contractions with comfortable pauses. Now: constant severe pain, pallor and faintness.
answers: The regular pattern means every later change is normal
Wait until the next planned check
Choose a named diagnosis before reporting
The sudden multi-clue change needs urgent qualified assessment
questions.explanation: A sudden change from regular contractions to constant severe pain with faintness requires urgent assessment.

questions.question: Which response addresses both risks?
questions.context: A newborn remains wet and feels cool. Breathing has also become irregular.
answers: Dry the newborn, support skin-to-skin warmth and obtain prompt qualified assessment for the breathing change
Leave wet coverings in place and wait
questions.explanation: Wet coverings increase heat loss, while irregular breathing is a concerning change requiring qualified assessment.

questions.question: What should happen before the clean task?
questions.context: The same gloves handled waste and are now reaching towards a clean cord-care pack.
answers: Keep the same gloves because they are intact
Touch the clean pack to test it
Remove contaminated gloves, perform hand hygiene and use appropriate clean equipment
Skip hand hygiene after removing gloves
questions.explanation: Waste-contaminated gloves must not move directly to a clean task; glove removal and hand hygiene address both risks.
